interest: American engineer's map helped Japanese attack Wau in New Guinea.
overview: 1945 correspondence on Joe Hofstetter, an American engineer in New Guinea credited on a map found on a Japanese officer killed at Wau.

people.name: Joe Hofstetter
people.role: Swiss engineer, naturalized U.S. citizen, former U.S. Coast Guard serviceman, and suspected collaborator with Japanese forces

people.name: F. W. R. Godden
people.role: General Manager of the Bulolo Gold Dredging Company Limited

people.name: John Bolger
people.role: U.S. Supervising Inspector 1st District, U.S. Department of Commerce

people.name: J. W. Mitchell
people.role: Commissioner for Affidavits and local Justice of the Peace at Bulolo

subfiles.about: Consular despatch reporting allegations that naturalized American and Swiss engineer Joe Hofstetter assisted Japanese forces during their attack on Wau, New Guinea.
subfiles.summary: Sydney reports that a map found on a dead Japanese officer at Wau credited Joe Hofstetter with trail data for a secret attack route.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1945 from American Consulate General Sydney: Reported Activities of Joe Hofstetter, alias Timothy Spur

subfiles.about: Sworn application and affidavit by Timothy Spot (Joe Hofstetter) requesting an American passport to travel to Manila to enlist in the U.S. Navy.
subfiles.summary: Timothy Spot (Joe Hofstetter) applies in 1941 for a passport to enlist in the U.S. Navy, describing his Coast Guard service.
subfiles.title: Letter and Affidavit of Timothy Spot (Joe Hofstetter) Applying for a U.S. Passport

subfiles.about: State Department transmittal sheet routing the Sydney consular report on Joe Hofstetter to the FBI and OSS.
subfiles.summary: State sends Sydney's despatch on Joe Hofstetter to the FBI and OSS.
subfiles.title: Department of State Transmittal Memorandum to FBI and OSS
subfiles.to: Federal Bureau of Investigation and Office of Strategic Services
